candidate.name: Lay of the Hidden King
candidate.rules:
I — Tap up to one target creature an opponent controls.
II — Up to one target creature you control gains ward {2} until your next turn.
III — Exile up to one target creature you control, then return it to the battlefield under its owner's control.
candidate.story: A song about Odysseus returning to his own household in disguise (Books XIII–XVII).
candidate.credit: Art: Greek, Melian, ca. 460–450 BCE · The Met
candidate.storyTarget: A song about Odysseus returning to his own household in disguise (Books XIII–XVII).
candidate.flavorStoryElement: A song about Odysseus returning to his own household in disguise (Books XIII–XVII).
candidate.flavorMatchRationale: Preserved as an ordinary WU Saga after leaving the hybrid song cycle. Its tap, ward and blink sequence remains a clean disguise-and-recognition story and no longer has to satisfy single-colour hybrid constraints.

candidate.name: A Name Kept Hidden
candidate.rules:
Face-down creatures you control have menace.
Whenever one or more face-down creatures you control deal combat damage to a player, surveil 2. This ability triggers only once each turn.
{3}{U}{B}: Manifest fate.
candidate.story: A concealed identity can be protection, weapon and source of dangerous knowledge; the hidden name and the hidden card share the same strategic space.
candidate.credit: Art: Giovanni Paolo Negroli · National Gallery of Art
candidate.flavorMatchRationale: Menace gives hidden creatures a route to connect; surveil turns successful disguise into graveyard selection; the mana sink self-enables.

candidate.name: Penelope's Unending Loom
candidate.rules:
Whenever you discard one or more cards, put a lore counter on this enchantment. This ability triggers only once each turn.
Remove three lore counters from this enchantment: Return target instant, sorcery, or enchantment card from your graveyard to your hand. Activate only as a sorcery.
candidate.story: Later reception / Penelope's weaving becomes a symbol not only of delay but of revision, authorship and repeatedly remaking the same story.
candidate.credit: Art: “Penelope” · John Roddam Spencer Stanhope · Private collection · Wikimedia Commons
candidate.storyTarget: Later reception / Penelope's weaving becomes a symbol not only of delay but of revision, authorship and repeatedly remaking the same story.
candidate.flavorStoryElement: Later reception / Penelope's weaving becomes a symbol not only of delay but of revision, authorship and repeatedly remaking the same story.
candidate.flavorMatchRationale: Discarded stories accumulate shared lore counters, which later recover a spell or enchantment.

candidate.name: The House Endures
candidate.rules:
At the beginning of your second main phase, if one or more creatures you control are tapped, put a +1/+1 counter on up to one target creature you control.
Whenever an enchantment you control enters, untap up to one target creature you control. This ability triggers only once each turn.
candidate.story: A functioning house survives absence because work continues: people tap themselves to labor, rituals repeat and the structure refreshes those who sustain it.
candidate.flavorMatchRationale: Both triggers are independently useful and together make GW's civilization-through-work identity explicit.

candidate.name: Memory Beneath the Earth
candidate.rules:
Whenever one or more permanent cards leave your graveyard, put a charge counter on this enchantment. This ability triggers only once each turn.
Remove three charge counters from this enchantment: Return target permanent card from your graveyard to your hand.
candidate.story: Burial does not erase relationship: graves, ancestors and recovered objects keep the past materially present beneath ordinary life.
candidate.credit: Art: “The Elysian Fields” · Arnold Böcklin · Kunst Museum Winterthur | Reinhart am Stadtgarten · Wikimedia Commons
candidate.flavorMatchRationale: Charge counters now track the repeated return of cards from the graveyard without a unique memory-counter type.
